sven: Quick heads-up — I found a perf + quality regression when switching Mixtral-8B to NTK RoPE for long contexts. Throughput drops ~18% and ppl increases ~0.9 at 6k+ tokens. Kernel selector log shows it falling back to the generic 'kv-shard-single' path for certain heads, which kills batching.

jamie: Can you paste the selector trace / perf sample? Was this on Dedicated or Private? @sven

sven: Private (on-prem test pool). Trace + snippet below.

sven: ```
[selector] model=mixtral-8b variant=ntk_rope seq=6144 batch=1 -> kernel=kv-shard-single
[perf] gen_tokens: 1.18ms/token (baseline 0.99ms)
[quality] ppl: 12.3 -> 13.2 (+0.9)
[mem] kv_alloc: 12.3GB -> 12.7GB (extra fragmentation)
```

soojae: I think this matches something I saw on Qwen-7B where linear->ntk toggles head remap and changes KV layout, causing extra memcpy. Batching heuristics can't merge caches across the new layout so continuous batching drops.

marie: From the runprofile it looks like the NTK exponent we used (1.25) pushes the rotation angles off the safe numeric range for Mixtral's rotary implementation. That causes the fallback to the generic kernel with a different kv stride. We should try clamping the ntk exponent per-model.

jamie: Good catch. Do we have a quick experiment to validate? Maybe try: ntk_exponent=1.0 (linear), 1.1, 1.15, 1.2 and check kernel choice + ppl.

sven: I ran a narrow sweep:
```
ntk=1.00 -> kernel=kv-shard-vec (good), ppl=12.3, throughput=1.00x
ntk=1.10 -> kernel=kv-shard-vec (good), ppl=12.4, throughput=0.98x
ntk=1.15 -> kernel=mixed (some heads remapped), ppl=12.7, throughput=0.94x
ntk=1.25 -> kernel=kv-shard-single (fallback), ppl=13.2, throughput=0.82x
```

soojae: That cliff at 1.15–1.25 suggests a per-head threshold where the rotation matrix becomes non-compatible with the packed-kv kernel. Could be dependent on head_dim too (Mixtral has 64 vs Llama's 128 in some configs).

marie: For safety, we should publish a per-model "safe RoPE exponent" table in runtime configs and let the kernel selector refuse exponents that cause layout incompatibility. For Mixtral-8B set max_ntk=1.15 for now.

jamie: Action items:
- sooj ae: run microbench across batch sizes [1,4,8], seqlens [2048,4096,6144,8192], record kernel outputs and memcpy counts
- jamie: add regression alert that fires when kernel_selector picks kv-shard-single AND token_latency increases >15%
- marie: add per-model clamp to config with a note for Mixtral/Qwen

sven: Temporary workaround for customers: set ropecfg.variant=linear or ropecfg.ntk=1.10 in model override. Example config snippet:
```
{"ropecfg":{"variant":"ntk","exponent":1.10}}
```

eng-deploy-bot: Deployment test for mixtral-ntk-clamp v1 applied to private-pool-23 — 2/2 nodes updated :white_check_mark:

soojae: Will kick off the sweep now and post a condensed CSV.

jamie: Thanks — please also capture kernel-selector debug logs (enable selector_debug=true) so we can identify exact remap rule that triggers fallback.

sven: Noted. If sweep reproduces across batch sizes we'll backport fix to the kernel compatibility check and add a perf guard in the runtime to prefer vec-shard kernels when head_dim==64 and ntk_exponent>1.12.

marie: Also add a small eval byprompt (long-form completion) to verify quality doesn't regress with the chosen clamp.

soojae: CSV upload: https://internal-storage/redwood/perf/mixtral-ntk-sweep-1764532109.csv (I'll ping when ready) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jamie: Great thread. Keeping this here for visibility — might need a dedicated postmortem if customers hit it in prod. :warning:
